o1.biggest_strength: It works out a real contribution-margin baseline (13.6% a year ago, 7.8% now) and sizes every move in points of margin, with the working shown. Each move has an owner, effort, week-4 and week-8 lines, and the scorecard carries action thresholds. This is what lets me rank by gross profit and effort.
o1.biggest_mistake: It is dense, and probably over the 1,600-word cap. Some claims are unsupported, such as the 'practitioner yardstick' for flows. The gain sizes rest on stacked assumptions, and the 'week 2 line' shorthand is cryptic.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim to the word limit and write the sizing in plainer words. Drop the unsourced benchmark. Give each move an explicit first-week step. Keep the 'proved' and 'to check' split and the baseline math.

o2.biggest_strength: It is clear and well organised. It separates proved from still-to-check, with an owner and a date on each check. The $94 payback rule per ad set and the per-channel payback math (Meta loses $27, Google breaks even, other makes $14) are sharp. The stop list is practical and fits the brand.
o2.biggest_mistake: It never computes the contribution-margin baseline, saying 'set baseline in week 1'. The impact of each move is mostly qualitative ('high', 'medium'), so the ranking by gross profit is weakly backed. The core-product return fixes are low value.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Compute the contribution baseline and put a number on each move's gain. Add a first-week action per move. Give the scorecard action thresholds, and put the Meta reset and flows ahead of the minor returns fixes.

reason: Output 1 gives me a real margin baseline, sized and ranked moves, owners, thresholds and a scorecard I can run Monday. Output 2 is easier to read but leaves the key numbers for me to figure out. I'd ask my team to trim Output 1 to the word limit and use it.
